attribution.text: John Owen, An Exposition of the Epistle of Paul the Apostle to the Hebrews, on chapters 1 and 2 (London, 1668) and on chapters 6 to 10 (London, 1680), in two volumes. Text keyed and encoded by the Early English Books Online Text Creation Partnership and dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0.

modifications: Converted from TEI XML to plain text paragraphs with emphasis. The two volumes are read as one book: chapters 1 and 2 from the first, and chapters 6 to 10 from the second. Owen expounds each verse or group of verses in its own division, headed as he printed it, such as Verse III. or Verse 4, 5, 6. In the first volume a section opens at each heading in Roman figures, such as Verse X, XI, XII., and the divisions after it, on the Greek text and its translations and labelled in Arabic figures, stay with it, so the notes on chapter 2 that the print labels verses 3, 4 and 5 stay with the heading on verses 2 to 4, whose text they quote. In the second volume sections are keyed by the verse numbers the transcription gives each division, at the first verse the division names, and divisions that open on the same verse share a section. A section runs from its own verse to the verse before the next section or the end of its chapter, so where Owen first expounds a group of verses together and then takes them one by one, the exposition of the group appears at its first verse. A chapter's introduction opens its first verse section, and in chapter 10, where the introduction runs on into the exposition of verse 1, it is the section on verse 1. Each marginal note moves to the section's notes. Every gap the transcribers could not key is kept as the mark they gave it, such as 〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉 for Greek or Hebrew, 〈◊〉 for an illegible word, and 〈1 page duplicate〉 for a page filmed twice. Line-end hyphens are closed up. Left out: Owen's Exercitations, bound before the exposition of chapters 1 and 2, with their dedication, epistle to the reader and errata; the title pages and prefaces; the headings such as AN EXPOSITION OF THE SIXTH CHAPTER and CHAP. I.; the closing End of the first Chapter. and FINIS; and the duplicate pages filmed after the second volume's FINIS. These volumes cover chapters 1 and 2 and 6 to 10 only, so the rest of Hebrews is not yet covered.
